title: German Schnitzel Gratin
description: A German-inspired take on French cuisine, this Schnitzel Gratin combines crispy breaded pork with a rich, creamy bechamel sauce.
instructions: Season the pork cutlets with salt and black pepper.
In a shallow dish, mix together the flour, a pinch of salt, and a few grinds of black pepper.
Dip each cutlet in the flour mixture, coating both sides evenly.
Dip the floured cutlet in the beaten egg, making sure to coat it completely.
Finally, roll the egg-coated cutlet in the bread crumb mixture to coat, pressing the crumbs gently onto the meat to ensure they stick.
Heat 2 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the breaded cutlets to the skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer the cooked cutlets to a baking dish and spoon some of the bechamel sauce over the top of each cutlet.
Sprinkle the grated Gruyère cheese over the top of each cutlet.
Transfer the baking dish to the preheated oven and bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the sauce is bubbly.
Remove the dish from the oven and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
